title: NOESY-based strategy for assignments of backbone and side chain resonances of large proteins without deuteration
protocol: Record 3D TROSY-HNCA, 3D MQ-CCH-TOCSY, and 4D ¹³C, ¹⁵N-edited NOESY for resonance assignment.
Use half-point delays for the evolution periods of Cα spins (t₁) in the HNCA.
Use half-point delays for the evolution periods of ¹³C spins (bonded with the directly detected ¹H, t₂) in the MQ-CCH-TOCSY.
Use half-point delays for both ¹³C and ¹⁵N spins (t₂ and t₃) in the 4D NOESY.
Record a 2D ¹H-¹⁵N TROSY-HSQC with sufficient spectral width in the ¹⁵N dimension to identify peaks aliased in the ¹⁵N dimension in 3D HNCA and 4D ¹³C, ¹⁵N-edited NOESY.
Process the data with NMRPipe.
Improve resolution of all indirectly detected dimensions using linear prediction.
Convert processed spectra into ucsf format for further analysis with Sparky.
Use peak picking functions in Sparky to pick HNCA peaks automatically.
Group HNCA peaks into clusters according to \(H^N, N\) chemical shifts.
Identify peaks from NH2 groups according to their paired patterns and unusual "C^α" chemical shifts.
Exclude identified NH2 group peaks during backbone assignment.
Check the number of clusters identified and ensure it matches the expected number.
Pick peaks in 4D ^13C,^15N-edited NOESY manually or automatically.
Group NOE peaks into their corresponding clusters according to \(H^N, N\) chemical shifts of individual clusters.
Correct chemical shifts of aliased peaks in 3D TROSY-HNCA and 4D NOESY with Sparky.
Pick peaks in CCH-TOCSY.
Initialize a spin-system from one HNCA peak in a given cluster.
Identify the NOE peak that matches the HNCA peak in 13C chemical shift within a certain tolerance (e.g., ~0.3 ppm).
Display the TOCSY slice defined by the H, C chemical shifts of each NOE peak in this cluster.
Check if the CH spin-pair of the NOE peak correlates with the Cα spin of this initial spin-system.
Regard the NOE peak as a sequential or intraresidue side chain NOE in this spin-system if the correlation is detected.
Verify that the 13C spin of the CH spin-pair correlates with CαHα of this spin-system via TOCSY.
Build two spin-systems using the two NOE peaks when only one HNCA peak is picked for a cluster due to degenerate Cα chemical shifts.
Separate the NOE peaks belonging to these two spin-systems based on side chain 13C spins correlating with two non-degenerate CαHα spin-pairs in CCH-TOCSY.
Check whether the CH spin-pairs correlate with each other in CCH-TOCSY for each spin-system.
Verify if the correlations can be explained by one of the 20 amino acids in terms of number of peaks and chemical shifts.
Classify a spin-system by residue type based on its Cα chemical shift and NOE peaks.
Identify glycine according to its small Cα chemical shift and sometimes two Hα peaks.
Recognize alanine based on its strong intraresidue CβHβ-NH NOE peak, strong Cα-CβHβ TOCSY peak, and characteristic Cα and Cβ chemical shifts.
Classify threonine, valine, isoleucine, and leucine based on their characteristic side chain chemical shifts.
Distinguish serine, lysine, arginine, and proline residues if the CβHβ spin-pair for serine, CβHβ, CγHγ and CδHδ spin-pairs for lysine, arginine, and proline can be identified.
Classify remaining residues into three groups based on 1H and 13C chemical shifts: (Asp, Asn, Phe, Tyr), (Gln, Glu, Met) and (Cys, Trp, His).
Link clusters to build fragments through matching spin-systems.
Match spin-systems when they have identical Cα chemical shifts.
Match spin-systems based on the largest number of matched NOE peaks.
Ensure no inconsistent (C, H) chemical shifts between matching spin-systems.
Compare spin-system types with the protein sequence for mapping fragments.
Map a fragment onto a segment of the sequence if residue types match at every position.
Consider the intraresidue HNCA peak strength to determine N-terminus in fragments.
Check mappings carefully if inconsistent with expected intra-residue and sequential correlations.
Resolve ambiguities in sequential connectivities using common NOEs shared by two clusters.
Repeat steps 11 to 13 iteratively.
Assign unassigned fragments and clusters in an iterative manner.
Recognize errors introduced during spin-system identification and classification.
Identify side chain chemical shifts based on identified spin-systems and backbone assignments.
Extend side chain resonance assignment by comparing two 13C,15N-edited NOESY planes defined by adjacent amides.
Explore MQ-CCH-TOCSY extensively for more extensive side chain resonance assignment.
Assign NH2 chemical shifts according to Cβ-NH2 and Cγ-NH2 correlations in the HNCA spectrum for asparagine and glutamine respectively.
Assign NH2 chemical shifts according to HβCβ-NH2 and HγCγ-NH2/HβCβ-NH2 correlations in the 4D 13C,15N-edited NOESY for asparagine and glutamine respectively.
Assign CδHδ groups of aromatic residues according to their NOE correlations with intraresidue and sequential amides.
Collect data for other aromatic resonances using a 4D 13C,13C-edited NOESY (7 days for data collection).
Collect data for other aromatic resonances using a 3D 15N/13C-simultaneous NOESY (3 days for data collection).
Assign other NOE peaks in the 4D 13C,15N-edited NOESY and 13C,13C-edited NOESY.
Follow the conventional procedure for NOE assignment and structure calculation.
